The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Bitcoin slides to 3-month low of $65,000 as analyst flags fourth capitulation wave. "They are now selling at the very price they wish they had taken advantage of three months ago," wrote James Check. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Ethereum scaling project MegaETH slashes staff by 20% as it pursues AI business. Decentralized Finance total value locked on MegaETH dropped significantly from over $245 million to $8.8 million. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Kazakhstan plans tokenized government bonds in first quarter after $22 million note sale. The plan follows Kazakhstan's first sale of tokenized central bank notes as the country expands its crypto market. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

UK, Singapore, and Thailand central banks test cross-border FX settlement as stablecoins gain ground. Project Meridian FX APAC said it demonstrated how transactions can be coordinated across conventional settlement systems and those built using blockchain technology. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Britain could turn wasted Scottish wind power into bitcoin to cut its $1.3 billion grid bill. Britain could use bitcoin mining to absorb surplus Scottish wind power and reduce payments to wind farms to halt generation, according to a Bitcoin Policy Institute report. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

A behind the scenes force may amplify bitcoin and ether price volatility. Both bitcoin and ether are trading in price ranges where market makers and dealers may add to market volatility. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $65,691 with a -4.51% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $1,834.41 with a -5.36% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

items.title: Cryptocurrency Regulation: A Guide to U.S. & Global Policies | Britannica Money
items.description:
Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it’s an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. In the United States, Congress has moved toward establishing federal oversight of stablecoins and digital asset markets. The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins, while broader market structure legislation known as the CLARITY Act advanced in Congress in 2026 but has yet to become law. [...] The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established the first federal regulatory framework for stablecoins in the United States. It limits who can issue stablecoins and requires issuers to maintain reserves backing the tokens they have issued, make monthly disclosures detailing the assets held in reserve, and comply with anti–money laundering and consumer protection requirements.

### What is the CLARITY Act? [...] United Kingdom. The U.K. began regulating cryptocurrency in 2020. In October 2023, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) introduced stricter rules on crypto advertising. The Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 also expanded oversight of stablecoins. A broader regulatory framework was approved in 2026 and is scheduled to take effect in October 2027, bringing activities including crypto trading, custody, staking, and stablecoin issuance under FCA oversight.

items.title: What is the GENUIS Act and what does it mean for stablecoins? | Fidelity
items.description:
The GENIUS (Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoin) Act was signed into law on July 18, 2025. The bill establishes the first regulatory guidelines for stablecoins in the US. For most crypto enthusiasts, it was a long-awaited, landmark moment—one they hope will lead to regulatory guidelines for the rest of the crypto industry.

So what does the GENIUS Act actually do? And what are its potential implications for crypto investors? Let’s explore the details. [...] ### Key takeaways

   The GENIUS Act establishes the first comprehensive regulatory guidelines for stablecoins in the US.
   The bill establishes rules for issuers and reserves.
   While GENIUS is a significant development, investors should also keep in mind regulations do not prevent crypto prices from falling. [...] Licensing and oversight requirements for stablecoin issuers. Under GENIUS, companies that issue stablecoins are required to register with a federal authority. Issuers with over $10 billion in stablecoin issuance face federal oversight, while smaller ones can opt for state regulation if their situations are substantially similar to the federal framework. Note that the Treasury issued a notice of proposed rulemaking on April 1, 2026 regarding principles for oversight.
